overview.text: Area measures how much two-dimensional space a flat region covers, and it is expressed in square units such as square centimeters, not linear units such as centimeters. It distinguishes the size of a region from the length of its boundary, making it useful for estimating flooring or paint. For familiar shapes, formulas use dimensions: a rectangle’s area is length times width, and a triangle’s is half its base times its height. For curved regions, calculus can approximate area by adding thin rectangles and taking a limit. A definite integral gives signed area (above the x-axis minus below it); total area counts both portions positively. In two dimensions, integrating 1 over a region gives its area.

key_facts.text: Area is measured in square units; perimeter measures the boundary in linear units.
A rectangle’s area is length × width; a triangle’s area is ½ × base × height.
For curved regions, sums of rectangle areas can approach the exact area as the rectangles become narrower and their number increases.
A definite integral gives signed area: area above the x-axis minus area below it. To get total area, count both portions positively.
A double integral of the constant function 1 over a plane region gives that region’s area.
